name: Strengen
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village in the Stanzer Tal with a traditional old town center and an ideal location along the Arlberg-Radweg.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Strengen am Arlberg is situated at an elevation of 1,012 meters in the sunny Stanzertal along the rushing Rosanna river, positioned halfway between Landeck and the world-renowned alpine resort of St. Anton am Arlberg. Home to approximately 1,200 residents in the district of Landeck, this charming clustered village serves as the tranquil gateway to the Stanzertal. The settlement clings to the steep, south-facing northern mountain slope, majestically flanked by the Lechtal Alps to the north – featuring peaks such as the Dawinkopf (2,968 m) and Eisenspitze (2,859 m) – and the Verwall Alps to the south. Strengen enchants visitors with its preserved rural architecture, historic wooden barns, and deep-rooted alpine tranquility, offering an idyllic base close to premier Arlberg sporting hubs.

Geschichte

The settlement of the Stanzertal has deep historical roots. Strengen was first documented in 1336 through a reference to Jakob der Streng, and later appeared as Gstreng in Peter Anich's landmark 1774 Atlas Tyrolensis. An exceptional testament to traditional alpine engineering is the heritage-listed covered wooden Strenger Brücke over the Rosanna river. Constructed in 1764 as an 18-meter-long timber truss structure, it was completed entirely with wooden pegs, containing neither iron nails nor metal bolts, and ranks among the oldest preserved covered bridges in Austria. The parish church dedicated to St. Martin von Tours stands prominently on a hillside shelf above the river; first mentioned in 1420, it was redesigned in Baroque style between 1753 and 1755 by master builder Paul Glatzl and received its spire in 1821. In the hamlet of Klaus, the 18th-century pilgrimage chapel Maria Hilf maintains a revered devotional tradition. Since the completion of the 5.85-kilometer-long Strenger Tunnel on the S16 expressway, through-traffic has been redirected underground, returning peace to the mountain village.

Anreise

Strengen enjoys excellent accessibility while remaining completely shielded from transit noise. Motorists reach the village via the Arlberg Schnellstraße S16 by taking the Strengen exit or the Flirsch/Pians junctions, continuing along the L68 Stanzertalstraße. Driving time is roughly 15 minutes from Landeck and 20 minutes from St. Anton am Arlberg. Train travelers arrive via the major railway stations of Landeck-Zams or St. Anton am Arlberg, which receive regular ÖBB Railjet and Eurocity trains. From both stations, VVT regional bus line 4242 operates frequent connections into the heart of Strengen. During winter, complimentary ski shuttles link the village directly with Arlberg cable car terminals. Cyclists can pedal along the Stanzertal cycle path beside the Rosanna river.

Tipps

A prime photography and architecture destination is the historic wooden bridge (Strenger Brücke) from 1764 spanning the churning waters of the Rosanna. Hikers can explore scenic paths along the Rosanna gorge or venture into the nearby Schnanner Klamm, equipped with suspension bridges and viewing walkways near rushing waterfalls. Rock climbers appreciate the climbing crags at Schnanner Klamm, reflecting the village's status as the hometown of world-class professional climber Barbara Zangerl. Rewarding mountain hikes include ascending to the rustic Dawinalm at 1,811 meters or tackling the summit ridge of the Eisenspitze. In winter, a 1.2-kilometer floodlit toboggan run provides family fun, making Strengen an affordable and peaceful sanctuary just minutes from the world-famous Ski Arlberg arena with its 300 kilometers of groomed pistes.
